bihar_raw_news.content: Support our Journalism 9th Anniversary: Free Tote & Mug Subscribe Home India Congress to launch movement in Bihar over unorganised workers’ rights India Congress to launch movement in Bihar over unorganised workers’ rights PTI 19 September, 2026 07:46 pm IST Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Follow Us : Text Size: A- A+ Patna, Sep 19 (PTI) Senior Congress leader Udit Raj on Saturday said the party would launch a movement in Bihar to fight for the rights of workers in the unorganised sector, alleging that the new employment guarantee scheme had taken away the legal right to work guaranteed under MGNREGA. Addressing a press conference here, Raj said the biggest issue facing the country was that of labourers and unorganised-sector workers. The former MP alleged that though the VB-G RAM G scheme would provide 125 days of employment instead of the 100 days guaranteed under MGNREGA, the fundamental difference is that employment under the old scheme was a legal right, which had been removed under the new system. Show Full Article The Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) is the country’s rural employment and development legislation enacted in December 2025 by the Centre. Its provisions came into force in Bihar from July 1 this year, replacing the older Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). “In a state like Bihar, where poverty and unemployment are serious problems, this will directly affect workers. The Congress party will launch a movement to fight for the rights of workers in the unorganised sector in Bihar,” Raj said. He, however, did not mention when the movement will be launched. Lack of adequate employment opportunities forces workers from the state to migrate to southern India, Punjab and other parts of the country, the Congress leader claimed. Democracy was being weakened, he alleged, asserting that protecting the Constitution was the responsibility of all citizens. “Bihar has given direction to several important movements for democracy and social justice. Congress workers in the state will have to further strengthen the struggle for democracy, the Constitution and social equality,” he said. Bihar Pradesh Congress Committee president Rajesh Ram said lakhs of workers employed in municipal corporations, government departments and various institutions faced issues related to wages, job security, social security, working conditions and labour rights. “The Congress has consistently raised its voice on these issues and will continue to do so,” he said. Ram said workers from SC, ST and other disadvantaged sections required special attention and should receive fair remuneration, dignity and their rights. bihar_raw_news.title: Tej Pratap Yadav intends to establish a 'darbaar' in the 'Rise & Fall 2' Penthouse - IANS LIVE
bihar_raw_news.content: Tej Pratap Yadav intends to establish a 'darbaar' in the 'Rise & Fall 2' Penthouse IANS September 19, 2026 3:04 PM Share on | Mumbai, Sep 19 (IANS) The son of veteran Bihar politician Lalu Prasad Yadav and a former Bihar minister, Tej Pratap Yadav, will be entering the unpredictable "Rise & Fall Season 2" Tower soon. Reflecting on the time when others may have celebrated seeing him shaken, the politician was seen invoking the might of a Bargad. Tej Pratap made a strong declaration of his strength in the clip, saying, "Jab hum udte samay dagmaya aur sab maje le rahe the par woh bhul gaye ke hum bargadh hai bargadh jiska daali se zyaada mazbood hai jadh aur issliye aa rahe hai Rise & Fall pe gardha udane. (“A lot of people enjoyed it when I wavered with flying; however, they forgot that I am like a banyan tree, whose roots are stronger than its branches, and that's why we are coming to Rise & Fall to stir things up).” Sharing his plans for his time in the Tower, he added, “Waha ke Penthouse pe kabza nahi karenge darbaar lagayenge aur raj karenge neeche wala Basement ke logowa ke upar. (I won't just occupy the penthouse there; we'll run a darbaar and rule over the people in the basement)". “Aur duniya ko batla dijiye humara parivaar pura Bihar hai. (And tell the world that the entire Bihar is our family)," Tej Pratap ended up declaring. Meanwhile, former Indian cricketer Virender Sehwag will be making his OTT debut as the host of "Rise and Fall Season 2". “Cricket has taught me one thing—no match is won before the final ball, and Rise and Fall Season 2 takes that unpredictability to another level. As a host, what excites me about this game is that there are no easy wins and no fixed positions,” he shared. "Rise & Fall Season 2" will premiere on 26th September and air every day at 12 PM, for free on Prime Video and the MX Player Android app. --IANS pm/

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today distributed more than 51 thousand appointment letters to newly appointed youth in various Government Organisations at the 20th Rozgar Mela this afternoon through video conferencing. Speaking on the occasion, Mr Modi said that in recent years, the Central government has consistently focused on equipping the youth with the skills and opportunities needed to prepare for the future. He said the government’s endeavour has also been to ensure that the education and skills of the country’s youth keep pace with the needs of the changing economy. Prime Minister Modi said the government is also working to rapidly expand employment opportunities in the private sector. He said, with this objective, the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana has been launched with an outlay of around one lakh crore. The scheme is expected to enable nearly two crore young people to enter the workforce for the first time. Mr Modi highlighted that under the initiative, the government is providing an incentive of up to 15 thousand rupees to youth securing their first jobs, while also incentivising employers to create additional employment opportunities. Prime Minister Modi said that India has signed Free Trade Agreements with nearly 40 countries in the past few years, which is opening new doors of opportunity for the country’s youth. He said, such trade agreements pave the way for new partnerships and markets for country’s entrepreneurs, and create new career possibilities for the youth. He said, the talent and skills of country’s youth have won the trust of the entire world. Mr Modi said that the world has great expectations from India’s innovators, entrepreneurs and its youth power. Prime Minister Modi said that India is today the world’s third largest startup ecosystem. He highlighted that today, nearly half of recognised startups are in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Mr Modi added that the youth from villages, towns, and smaller cities are playing a significant role in India’s new economy. The Prime Minister highlighted that young people from smaller cities are working on their ideas, founding new companies, and creating employment opportunities for others. On the occasion, Minister of State for Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions Dr Jitendra Singh said that an assessment of employment generation and recruitment through Rozgar Mela has shown that there has been a significant increase in government appointments, along with the greater transparency. He said that nearly ten lakh 96 thousand appointments were made during the ten years of the NDA government as compared to seven lakh 22 thousand appointments during UPA government through three major central recruitment agencies – Union Public Service Commission, the Staff Selection Commission and the Railway Recruitment Boards. The Minister said several measures have been taken to improve the recruitment system. The 20th Rozgar Mela was held at 45 locations across the country. The newly recruited candidates will be joining various Ministries and Departments of the Government of India including, Ministries of Finance, Railways, Home Affairs, Health and Family Welfare, and Defence, among others. With the 20th Rozgar Mela, a total of about 12 lakh 75 thousand youths have received appointment letters. The Rozgar Mela reflects the Government’s continued focus on creating employment opportunities for the youth and ensuring their greater participation in the country’s development journey.

national_raw_news.title: 4 mins ago | National 273 PM Modi says India’s per capita carbon emissions less than half of global average
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that India’s contribution to per capita carbon emissions is less than half of the global average. Inaugurating the International Conference on the Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics in New Delhi today, Mr Modi said that developing countries have often been unfairly held responsible for carbon emissions. He highlighted that India is the only country in the G-20 that has successfully fulfilled the commitments made at the COP-21 Summit in Paris ahead of schedule. The Prime Minister said, over the past twelve years, India has made extraordinary progress in every field related to the environment. Prime Minister Modi said India is working with the rest of the world and setting new standards for environmental protection through initiatives such as the International Solar Alliance, Global Biofuels Alliance, International Big Cat Alliance and Mission LiFE. Mr Modi said that over the past twelve years, India has made extraordinary progress in every field related to the environment. The Prime Minister said, India’s major focus has been on renewable energy, and played a significant role in environmental protection. Prime Minister Modi said that India is rapidly working in areas like clean mobility and green hydrogen today. He highlighted that India’s wind energy capacity has witnessed three times growth in the last 12 years. Mr Modi emphasized that new India is also focusing on nuclear energy generation. On the occasion, Chief Justice of India, Surya Kant said that the idea of preserving the Earth existed in the country much before the emergence of environmental tribunals, regulatory mechanisms and compliance frameworks. He underlined the importance of the fundamental duty of every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures. The Chief Justice said that India’s Constitution is not merely a political document but also a moral commitment towards past, present and future generations. Speaking on the occasion, Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupender Yadav said that India’s approach to environmental responsibility is deeply rooted in its ancient civilizational ethos, which regards the Earth not as a possession but as a shared inheritance and a sacred trust. He said non-fossil fuel sources now account for more than 54 percent of India’s installed electricity capacity, surpassing the earlier target. Mr Yadav said India ranks third globally in renewable energy installed capacity and is the world’s second-largest solar growth market. Mr. Yadav added that these achievements demonstrate that economic growth and determined climate action can progress together. On wildlife conservation, the Minister said India’s efforts are not limited to protecting individual animals but are aimed at safeguarding the entire ecological balance. He said the populations of key species, including tigers, lions and elephants, have increased significantly, while efforts are also being intensified to conserve vultures and the Great Indian Bustard. Mr. Yadav also highlighted India’s efforts towards conservation and restoration of forests, grasslands and wetlands. The two-day conference is being organised by the National Green Tribunal. It has brought together environmental experts, judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, and District Court judges. It will also bring together eminent judges and judicial representatives from 17 countries. The Conference will provide a platform to exchange judicial approaches, scientific knowledge, environmental governance practices and institutional experiences. During the conference, participants will discuss key environmental and climate challenges, including gaps in policy formulation, implementation and enforcement. The conference will also explore ways to strengthen environmental governance and institutional cooperation.

national_raw_news.content: JP Nadda reviews health sector progress in Madhya Pradesh; commends state’s healthcare expansion and PPP model Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर JP Nadda reviews health sector progress in Madhya Pradesh; commends state’s healthcare expansion and PPP model ANI | Updated: Sep 18, 2026 21:59 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 18 (ANI): Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare JP Nadda met Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav on Friday to review the progress of the health sector in the State, with discussions focusing on healthcare infrastructure, medical education, specialised services and key public health initiatives. According to an official release, during the meeting, Nadda appreciated the Madhya Pradesh Government for its sustained efforts to strengthen the State’s healthcare ecosystem and expand access to quality healthcare. He particularly commended the State for leveraging the Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model to accelerate the expansion of medical education and healthcare infrastructure. A key focus of the review was the expansion of medical education in the State. Madhya Pradesh has increased its MBBS seats from 5,600 to 6,120 in 2026, adding 520 seats in a year. The State has also expanded super-speciality education, with seats in government medical colleges increasing from 63 to 73, and in private medical colleges from 29 to 53, the release mentioned. According to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Nadda appreciated these efforts, emphasising that expansion of medical education and specialist capacity will strengthen the healthcare workforce and improve the availability of advanced healthcare services across the State. The Union Health Minister also lauded Madhya Pradesh for its innovative use of the PPP model for establishing medical colleges. Under the initiative, medical colleges are being established in Dhar, Panna, Katni and Betul, with the institutions targeted for establishment by December 2027. The initiative represents an important step towards expanding medical education and bringing specialised healthcare services closer to people across different regions of the State. Nadda appreciated the State Government’s approach of combining public investment with private-sector participation to augment healthcare capacity and accelerate infrastructure development. The meeting also reviewed improvements in key maternal and child health indicators. As per SRS 2022–24, Madhya Pradesh’s Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) declined by 7 points to 135 per lakh live births. The proportion of pregnant women receiving four or more ANC visits increased from 57.5% to 69.5%, as per NFHS-6. Child health indicators have also shown improvement, with the Neonatal Mortality Rate declining from 27 to 26 and the Infant Mortality Rate from 37 to 35 per 1,000 live births. The State has also strengthened access to specialised healthcare. 70 haemodialysis units are operational across 52 districts, while 52 cancer day-care centres are providing cancer treatment services. Advanced cancer treatment facilities, including CAR-T cell therapy, have also been introduced at Government Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Medical College, Indore. The expansion of medical education infrastructure is further supported by new government medical colleges.
